D.label: PULL BENCH ROOM
D.name: Door to the pull bench room
D.text: The door to the bench room. It opens once you have read the picture card.

U.label: PULL BENCH
U.name: Pull bench
U.text: The pull bench: a model atom, a dial and a screen. Pick an atom, measure how hard its outer electron is held, and find what changes it. Press E to use it.

P.label: TABLE
P.name: Periodic table chart
P.text: A wall chart of the first twenty elements. Position on the chart tells you the period and the group.

K.label: BOARD
K.name: Chalkboard
K.text: Chalkboard: 'Who holds on harder: the nucleus, or the crowd in between?'

V.label: STATIC
V.name: Van de Graaff generator
V.text: A Van de Graaff generator. It piles charge onto the big sphere until the charge jumps to the small ball as a spark. Opposite charges pull on each other, and the pull gets weaker with distance.

H.name: Atom models
H.text: Ball-and-ring models of atoms on a shelf. The red ball is the nucleus. Each ring is a shell of electrons.

M.name: Magnet table
M.text: A horseshoe magnet and iron filings. Pull a magnet away and it fights you. Move it twice as far and the fight gets much weaker. Atoms hold their electrons by a pull like this one.

Y.name: Plant
Y.text: A plant. It is not on the quiz.

N.label: NOTICE
N.name: Notice board
N.text: Notice: 'The pull is a classroom number. It ranks atoms; it is not a measurement.'

S.label: MODELS
S.name: Atom models
S.text: Ball-and-ring models of atoms on a shelf. The red ball is the nucleus. Each ring is a shell of electrons.
